[5] For the reasons that follow, I find that XXXX XXXX has not satisfied the burden of establishing a serious possibility of persecution on a Convention ground, or that, on a balance of probabilities, she would personally be subjected to a risk to life or a risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment or a danger of torture upon return to China.

[6] Ms. XXXX allegations are set out in her narrative in the Basis of Claim form2 and were elaborated upon in oral testimony. Briefly, Ms. XXXX is 50 years of age and lived in XXXX, China. On several occasions in 2015 and 2016, Ms. XXXX travelled to Hong Kong and purchased books authored by a political dissident, which she then smuggled back to mainland China and sold for profit. Ms. XXXX later took a recreational trip to Canada in XXXX, 2017, and also visited the United States during that time. While speaking to her mother on the telephone from Canada on XXXX XXXX, 2017, she learned that members of the Public Service Bureau ("PSB") in China were searching for her. She made her claim for refugee protection on October 12, 2017.

Identity

[7] I find on a balance of probabilities that Ms. XXXX is the person she purports to be as well as a national of China. I rely on her testimony and the certified true copy of her Chinese passport which includes a Canadian visa.3

[8] The determinative issue in this matter is credibility.
Ms. XXXX testimony was not Believable

[9] I find that Ms. XXXX is not a credible witness. She misrepresented personal information on her application for a Canadian visa4, application for an American visa5, as well as on her application for permanent residence in Canada under the spousal sponsorship category6 - a process occurring concurrently with her claim for refugee protection. Minster's counsel asked Ms. XXXX about several inconsistencies and omissions in these documents regarding Ms. XXXX family composition. Ms. XXXX stated that she had legal counsel, her friend, or a lawyer's assistant prepared these documents on her behalf in China. Ms. XXXX stated that if the applications contained mistakes, then she was unaware of them. She also appeared to be unconcerned with the gravity of these discrepancies. Her reaction was quite similar to her apparent lack of knowledge and concern about the seriousness of her alleged book smuggling, noted below.

subthemes.text:
[10] I do not accept Ms. XXXX explanation for the numerous discrepancies found in her immigration documents. Ms. XXXX misrepresentations on official applications to foreign governments are serious and cannot simply be dismissed as clerical errors made by third parties. Ms. XXXX made these applications to foreign governments and whether they were completed by her or not, she is responsible for the content within those applications. She made each of the applications for pleasure, as she was not wanted by the Chinese authorities at the time of application.

[11] I note in particular that Ms. XXXX stated in her application for permanent residence that she did not have any criminal history in China. Through her mother, Ms. XXXX provided a notarial certificate7 from China purporting to corroborate this.8 This is in stark contrast to Ms. XXXX allegation in her claim for refugee protection that the Chinese authorities are searching for her because of her criminal book smuggling activities. If Ms. XXXX was wanted by the Chinese authorities for criminal activity, it is unreasonable to believe that she would be able to produce an official document stating that she has no criminal involvement.

[12] Ms. XXXX appears to have few qualms about misrepresenting herself to foreign governments and little to no regard to the veracity of personal information she provides. I do not accept her explanations that these mistakes were made by third parties or the result of a misunderstanding on her part. I draw a negative inference about Ms. XXXX credibility.
Ms. XXXX is not wanted by Chinese authorities in the manner alleged

[13] Ms. XXXX alleges that the PSB attended her mother's house in China in XXXX 2017. The PSB was searching for Ms. XXXX due to her alleged book smuggling, which, incidentally and unbelievably, Ms. XXXX stated she never realized was illegal or potentially dangerous. There is no proof that the Chinese authorities are interested in Ms. XXXX. She did not provide a letter from her mother corroborating this allegation, and surprisingly, failed to obtain and provide a letter in the four intervening months between hearing dates in this claim. In fact, Ms. XXXX provided little to no corroborating documents which would be reasonably expected in this matter: a letter from her mother; any paper from the PSB, such as a warrant or summons; receipts from her bookstore purchases, if available, a letter or affidavit from friends or neighbours and a letter or personal appearance from her Canadian husband. Ms. XXXX did not provide reasonable, if any, explanations for her lack of corroborating documents, which is curious, as she purportedly obtained the police clearance for her permanent residence application with the assistance of her mother. I draw a negative inference with regard to Ms. XXXX credibility insofar as she has failed to provide any reliable evidence to corroborate her allegation that she is at risk in China.

[14] I do not accept Ms. XXXX allegation that she is wanted by the Chinese authorities as she has provided no corroborating documents and no reasonable explanation for her failure to do so. I find that she is not wanted by the Chinese authorities in the manner alleged, if at all. I also draw a negative inference with regard to her credibility.
No Credible Basis

[15] Ms. XXXX oral testimony was as a whole, on a balance of probabilities, neither trustworthy nor credible. When a panel determines not only that the evidence adduced is insufficient to establish the claim, but also that there is no credible or trustworthy evidence on which the claim could have been accepted, the "no credible basis" provision is used.

If the Refugee Protection Division is of the opinion, in rejecting a claim, that there was no credible or trustworthy evidence on which it could have made a favourable decision, it shall state in its reasons for the decision that there is no credible basis for the claim.
CONCLUSION

[17] Accordingly I find, on a balance of probabilities, that XXXX XXXX has not established her claim on the basis of credible and trustworthy evidence and has not established the central element of her claim: that she is wanted by authorities in China.
